Dear Secretary Reese:

        Pursuant to Section 205 of the Federal Power Act (“FPA”), 16 U.S.C. § 824d,
and Section 35.13 of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission’s (“Commission”)
Regulations, 18 C.F.R. § 35.13, Southwest Power Pool, Inc. ("SPP") submits revisions
to Schedule 15 and Attachment T of its Open Access Transmission Tariff (“Tariff”)1
to add provisions for Conditional High Impact Large Load Service (“CHILLS”) for
pricing Zones in the SPP West Region, and to make other clarifying edits.

        SPP respectfully requests that the Commission accept the proposed revisions,
find the revisions just and reasonable, and set an effective date of February 1, 2027.

I.     BACKGROUND

       A.     SPP’s Regional Transmission Organization Expansion

      On April 1, 2026, SPP expanded its Regional Transmission Organization
(“RTO”) into the Western Interconnection.2 Specifically, the following utilities now

       revisions proposed in this filing. All capitalized terms not otherwise defined in
       this filing shall have the definitions assigned by the Tariff.
2

Basin Electric Power Cooperative (“Basin Electric”); Colorado Springs Utilities

(“Tri-State”); Western Area Power Administration – Colorado River Storage Project
Management Center (“WAPA-CRSP”); Western Area Power Administration – Rocky
Mountain Region (“WAPA-RMR”); and Western Area Power Administration – Upper

       At the time of the CHILLS Filing, the new pricing Zones for the SPP West
Region had not yet been established in the Tariff. SPP submits this filing to include the
pricing Zones in Schedule 15 of the Tariff, and to also add CHILLS provisions to

II.    DESCRIPTION OF AND JUSTIFICATION FOR PROPOSED TARIFF
       REVISIONS

       A.      Schedule 15

       In the CHILLS Filing, SPP proposed a new Schedule 15, to establish charges
for CHILLS.8 SPP proposes to add pricing Zones 100, 101, 102, 103, and 104 under
Section 1 of Schedule 15:

               Zone 100:       Colorado Springs Utilities
               Zone 101:       Platte River Power Authority
               Zone 102:       Tri-State G&T Association – West
               Zone 103:       Colorado River Storage Project Zone
               Zone 104:       Loveland Area Projects Zone

         These revisions are just and reasonable because they effectuate the intent of the
CHILLS Filing already accepted by the Commission and will allow those entities in
the SPP West Region that take CHILLS to also pay for the use of the transmission
facilities located in those newly formed Zones in the SPP West Region.

       B.      Attachment T

        Attachment T includes the rate sheets for Point-To-Point Transmission Service
for all applicable Transmission Owners under the Tariff. SPP proposes to revise the
following rate sheets.

               1.      Rate Sheets for CSU, Platte River, and WAPA-CRSP

and WAPA-CRSP:

               Large Load Service Revenue Crediting for Point-To-Point Rates

               Schedule 15 revenues, and revenues distributed and allocated under

               this Tariff. The rates, including any applicable adjustments for
               Schedule 7 and 8 revenues, and Schedule 15 revenues, and revenues

        Second, SPP adds a reference to Schedule 15 to appropriately adjust the Point-

        Third, SPP adds a reference to Incremental Market Efficiency Use revenues.

SCHEDULE 15
                CONDITIONAL HIGH IMPACT LARGE LOAD SERVICE

        For each Point of Delivery of the Conditional High Impact Large Load Service
(“CHILLS”), the Transmission Customer and Network Customer must compensate the
Transmission Provider for the CHILLS up to the monthly sum of the applicable charges set forth
below in addition to other applicable charges specified in the Tariff. All effective rates under
this schedule will be posted in the Revenue Requirements and Rates File (“RRR File”) on the
SPP website.


       1.     Zonal Rates per Kilowatt: The Transmission Customer and Network Customer
must pay the zonal rate (per kilowatt) based upon the Zone where the load is located for the
CHILLS. The zonal rate will be the hourly rate applicable to Non-Firm Point-To-Point
Transmission Service for the specific on-peak or off-peak hour of the CHILLS usage. For each
hour without Curtailment, the hourly charge will be calculated using kilowatts of the CHILLS
Reserved Capacity. For each hour with Curtailment, the hourly charge will be calculated using
the Curtailment kilowatt limit specified by the Transmission Provider. CHILLS load exceeding
the Curtailment limit specified by the Transmission Provider or the CHILLS Reserved Capacity
is subject to additional charges and penalties pursuant to Part VII, Section 44.4 of this Tariff.

       The Zones are as follows:
Zone 1: American Electric Power – West
Zone 2: Kansas City Board of Public Utilities
Zone 3: City Utilities of Springfield, Missouri
Zone 4: Empire District Electric Company
Zone 5: Grand River Dam Authority
Zone 6: Evergy Metro, Inc.
Zone 7: Oklahoma Gas & Electric Company
Zone 8: Midwest Energy, Inc.
Zone 9: Evergy Missouri West, Inc.
Zone 10: Southwestern Power Administration
Zone 11: Southwestern Public Service
Zone 12: Sunflower Electric Power Corporation
Zone 13: Western Farmers Electric Cooperative
 Zone 14: Evergy Kansas Central, Inc. (Evergy Kansas Central, Inc. and Evergy Kansas South,
         Inc.)
Zone 15: Reserved for Future Use
Zone 16: Lincoln Electric System
Zone 17: Nebraska Public Power District
Zone 18: Omaha Public Power District
Zone 19: Upper Missouri Zone
Zone 100: Colorado Springs Utilities
Zone 101: Platte River Power Authority
Zone 102: Tri-State G&T Association – West
Zone 103: Colorado River Storage Project Zone
Zone 104: Loveland Area Projects Zone
No changes in Zones will be made without submitting a filing to the Commission.


       2.    Caps: The total demand charge in any month for usage up to the CHILLS
Reserved Capacity will not exceed the monthly rate times the amount in kilowatts of CHILLS
Reserved Capacity in such month.


       3.     Redispatch Costs: The redispatch costs will be calculated in accordance with the
formula and protocols shown in Attachment K.


        4.     Discounts: The Transmission Provider may offer discounts under this
Schedule. Three principal requirements apply to discounts for transmission service as
follows: (1) any offer of a discount made by the Transmission Provider must be announced to all
Eligible Customers solely by posting on the OASIS, (2) any customer-initiated requests for
discounts must occur solely by posting on the OASIS, and (3) once a discount is negotiated,
details must be immediately posted on the OASIS. For any discount agreed upon for service to a
Point(s) of Delivery, the Transmission Provider must offer the same discounted CHILLS rate for
the same time period to all Eligible Customers on all unconstrained transmission paths that go to
the same Point(s) of Delivery on the Transmission System. In offering discounts, the
Transmission Provider’s goal will be to maximize transmission revenues.

       5.      Real Power Losses: The Transmission Customer and Network Customer will be
responsible for real power losses determined in accordance with Attachment M and Part VII,
Section 45.4 of this Tariff.
        6.      Wholesale Distribution Service: Where Wholesale Distribution Service is
provided to effectuate CHILLS, the Transmission Customer and Network Customer must pay all
charges levied pursuant to the Wholesale Distribution Service Agreement and Schedule 10.


       7.      Base Plan Zonal Charges, Subregional Charge, and Region-wide
Charges: The Transmission Customer and Network Customer must pay the applicable Schedule
11 zonal rate (per kilowatt) based upon the Zone where the load is located, the applicable
Schedule 11 Subregional Charge (per kilowatt) based upon the Subregion where the load is
located, and the applicable Schedule 11 region-wide rate for CHILLS. The rates will be the
applicable point-to-point hourly rates for the specific on-peak or off-peak hour of CHILLS
usage. The hourly charges will be calculated using hourly kilowatts as stated in Section 1 of
Schedule 15. The total Schedule 11 zonal charge in any month for usage up to the CHILLS
Reserved Capacity will not exceed the Schedule 11 point-to-point zonal monthly rate times the
amount in kilowatts of CHILLS Reserved Capacity in such month. The total Schedule 11 region-
wide charge in any month for usage up to the CHILLS Reserved Capacity will not exceed the
Schedule 11 point-to-point region-wide rate times the amount of kilowatts of CHILLS Reserved
Capacity in such month.

       8.     Resales: Resales are not permissible for CHILLS.
                                    Colorado Springs Utilities

                      Rate Sheet for Point-To-Point Transmission Service



         The currently effective rates for Point-To-Point Transmission Service in the Colorado
Spring Utilities (“CSU”) rate Zone are set forth in the “CSU PTP Rate Att T” tab of the Revenue
Requirements and Rates File (“RRR File”) posted on the SPP website.


Balanced Portfolio Reallocation Adjustment of Point-To-Point Rates
         Rates for Point-To-Point Transmission Service specified in this Attachment T shall be
adjusted to reflect any amount reallocated from the Zonal Annual Transmission Revenue
Requirement in accordance with Section IV.A of Attachment J.           The rates, including any
applicable reallocation adjustment, shall be set forth in the RRR File posted on the SPP website.


Point-To-Point Transmission Service and Conditional High Impact Large Load Service
Revenue Crediting for Point-To-Point Rates
         Rates for Point-To-Point Transmission Service under this Attachment T shall reflect any
adjustments for Schedule 7 and 8 revenues, and Schedule 15 revenues, and revenues distributed
and allocated under Attachment AU, implemented in accordance with Section 34.1(2) of this
Tariff. The rates, including any applicable adjustments for Schedule 7 and 8 revenues, and
Schedule 15 revenues, and revenues distributed and allocated under Attachment AU, shall be set
forth in the RRR File.


Firm Point-To-Point Transmission Service
         The Transmission Customer shall compensate the Transmission Provider each month for
Reserved Capacity at the sum of the applicable charges set forth in the RRR File, calculated
pursuant to the CSU formula rate shown in Attachment H, Addendum XX54 and described
below:
1.       Yearly delivery: one-twelfth of the rate per MW of Reserved Capacity per year.
2.       Monthly delivery: rate per MW of Reserved Capacity per month.
3.       Weekly delivery: rate per MW of Reserved Capacity per week.
4.       Daily on-peak delivery: rate per MW of Reserved Capacity per day.
 5.     Daily off-peak delivery: rate per MW of Reserved Capacity per day.


       The total demand charge in any week, pursuant to a reservation for Daily delivery, shall
not exceed the rate specified for Weekly delivery multiplied by the highest amount in megawatts
of Reserved Capacity in any day during such week.


Non-Firm Point-To-Point Transmission Service
       The Transmission Customer shall compensate the Transmission Provider for Non-Firm
Point-To-Point Transmission Service up to the sum of the applicable charges set forth in the
RRR File, calculated pursuant to the CSU formula rate shown in Attachment H, Addendum 4654
and described below:
1.     Monthly delivery: rate per MW of Reserved Capacity per month.
2.     Weekly delivery: rate per MW of Reserved Capacity per week.
3.     Daily on-peak delivery: rate per MW of Reserved Capacity per day.
4.     Daily off-peak delivery: rate per MW of Reserved Capacity per day.
5.     Hourly on-peak delivery: rate per MW of Reserved Capacity per hour.
6.     Hourly off-peak delivery: rate per MW of Reserved Capacity per hour.
       The total demand charge in any day, pursuant to a reservation for Hourly delivery, shall
not exceed the rate specified for Daily on-peak delivery multiplied by the highest amount in
megawatts of Reserved Capacity in any hour during such day. In addition, the total demand
charge in any week, pursuant to a reservation for Hourly or Daily delivery, shall not exceed the
rate specified for Weekly delivery multiplied by the highest amount in megawatts of Reserved
Capacity in any hour during such week.
                                    Loveland Area Projects
                     Rate Sheet for Point-To-Point Transmission Service



The currently effective rates for Point-To-Point Transmission Service in the Loveland Area
Projects (“LAP”) rate Zone are set forth in the “LAP PTP Rate Att T” tab of the Revenue
Requirements and Rates File (“RRR File”) posted on the SPP website. Transmission Owners(s)
that have Commission approved rate(s) in the LAP rate Zone are: Western Area Power
Administration-Rocky Mountain Region (“WAPA-RMR”), Platte River Power Authority
(“PRPA”), and Tri-State G&T Association-West (“TSGT-West”).




Balanced Portfolio Reallocation Adjustment of Point-To-Point Rates
       Rates for Point-To-Point Transmission Service specified in this Attachment T shall be
adjusted to reflect any amount reallocated from the Zonal Annual Transmission Revenue
Requirement in accordance with Section IV.A of Attachment J.           The rates, including any
applicable reallocation adjustment, shall be set forth in the RRR File posted on the SPP website.


Point-To-Point Transmission Service Revenue Crediting for Point-To-Point Rates
       Rates for Point-To-Point Transmission Service under this Attachment T shall reflect any

revenues, and revenues distributed and allocated under Attachment AU, implemented in

       The Transmission Customer shall compensate the Transmission Provider each month for

pursuant to the WAPA-RMR, PRPA, and TSGT-West formula rate shown in Attachment H,

Reserved Capacity. For each hour with Curtailment, the hourly charge will be calculated using
the Curtailment kilowatt limit specified by the Transmission Provider. CHILLS load exceeding
the Curtailment limit specified by the Transmission Provider or the CHILLS Reserved Capacity is
subject to additional charges and penalties pursuant to Part VII, Section 44.4 of this Tariff.

       2.      Caps: The total demand charge in any month for usage up to the CHILLS Reserved
Capacity will not exceed the monthly rate times the amount in kilowatts of CHILLS Reserved
Capacity in such month.


       3.     Redispatch Costs: The redispatch costs will be calculated in accordance with the
formula and protocols shown in Attachment K.


        4.     Discounts: The Transmission Provider may offer discounts under this
Schedule. Three principal requirements apply to discounts for transmission service as
follows: (1) any offer of a discount made by the Transmission Provider must be announced to all
Eligible Customers solely by posting on the OASIS, (2) any customer-initiated requests for
discounts must occur solely by posting on the OASIS, and (3) once a discount is negotiated, details
must be immediately posted on the OASIS. For any discount agreed upon for service to a Point(s)
of Delivery, the Transmission Provider must offer the same discounted CHILLS rate for the same
time period to all Eligible Customers on all unconstrained transmission paths that go to the same
Point(s) of Delivery on the Transmission System. In offering discounts, the Transmission
Provider’s goal will be to maximize transmission revenues.

       5.      Real Power Losses: The Transmission Customer and Network Customer will be
responsible for real power losses determined in accordance with Attachment M and Part VII,
Section 45.4 of this Tariff.
        6.      Wholesale Distribution Service: Where Wholesale Distribution Service is
provided to effectuate CHILLS, the Transmission Customer and Network Customer must pay all
charges levied pursuant to the Wholesale Distribution Service Agreement and Schedule 10.


        7.      Base Plan Zonal Charges, Subregional Charge, and Region-wide Charges: The
Transmission Customer and Network Customer must pay the applicable Schedule 11 zonal rate
(per kilowatt) based upon the Zone where the load is located, the applicable Schedule 11
Subregional Charge (per kilowatt) based upon the Subregion where the load is located, and the
applicable Schedule 11 region-wide rate for CHILLS. The rates will be the applicable point-to-
point hourly rates for the specific on-peak or off-peak hour of CHILLS usage. The hourly charges

11 zonal charge in any month for usage up to the CHILLS Reserved Capacity will not exceed the
Schedule 11 point-to-point zonal monthly rate times the amount in kilowatts of CHILLS Reserved
Capacity in such month. The total Schedule 11 region-wide charge in any month for usage up to
the CHILLS Reserved Capacity will not exceed the Schedule 11 point-to-point region-wide rate
times the amount of kilowatts of CHILLS Reserved Capacity in such month.

                                SCHEDULE 15
                CONDITIONAL HIGH IMPACT LARGE LOAD SERVICE

       For each Point of Delivery of the Conditional High Impact Large Load Service
(“CHILLS”), the Transmission Customer and Network Customer must compensate the
Transmission Provider for the CHILLS up to the monthly sum of the applicable charges set forth
below in addition to other applicable charges specified in the Tariff. All effective rates under this
schedule will be posted in the Revenue Requirements and Rates File (“RRR File”) on the SPP
website.


        1.      Zonal Rates per Kilowatt: The Transmission Customer and Network Customer
must pay the zonal rate (per kilowatt) based upon the Zone where the load is located for the
CHILLS. The zonal rate will be the hourly rate applicable to Non-Firm Point-To-Point
Transmission Service for the specific on-peak or off-peak hour of the CHILLS usage. For each
hour without Curtailment, the hourly charge will be calculated using kilowatts of the CHILLS
Reserved Capacity. For each hour with Curtailment, the hourly charge will be calculated using the
Curtailment kilowatt limit specified by the Transmission Provider. CHILLS load exceeding the
Curtailment limit specified by the Transmission Provider or the CHILLS Reserved Capacity is
subject to additional charges and penalties pursuant to Part VII, Section 44.4 of this Tariff.

       2.      Caps: The total demand charge in any month for usage up to the CHILLS Reserved
Capacity will not exceed the monthly rate times the amount in kilowatts of CHILLS Reserved
Capacity in such month.


       3.     Redispatch Costs: The redispatch costs will be calculated in accordance with the
formula and protocols shown in Attachment K.


        4.     Discounts: The Transmission Provider may offer discounts under this
Schedule. Three principal requirements apply to discounts for transmission service as
follows: (1) any offer of a discount made by the Transmission Provider must be announced to all
Eligible Customers solely by posting on the OASIS, (2) any customer-initiated requests for
discounts must occur solely by posting on the OASIS, and (3) once a discount is negotiated, details
must be immediately posted on the OASIS. For any discount agreed upon for service to a Point(s)
of Delivery, the Transmission Provider must offer the same discounted CHILLS rate for the same
time period to all Eligible Customers on all unconstrained transmission paths that go to the same
Point(s) of Delivery on the Transmission System. In offering discounts, the Transmission
Provider’s goal will be to maximize transmission revenues.


       5.      Real Power Losses: The Transmission Customer and Network Customer will be
responsible for real power losses determined in accordance with Attachment M and Part VII,
Section 45.4 of this Tariff.

provided to effectuate CHILLS, the Transmission Customer and Network Customer must pay all
charges levied pursuant to the Wholesale Distribution Service Agreement and Schedule 10.


        7.      Base Plan Zonal Charges, Subregional Charge, and Region-wide Charges: The
Transmission Customer and Network Customer must pay the applicable Schedule 11 zonal rate
(per kilowatt) based upon the Zone where the load is located, the applicable Schedule 11
Subregional Charge (per kilowatt) based upon the Subregion where the load is located, and the
applicable Schedule 11 region-wide rate for CHILLS. The rates will be the applicable point-to-
point hourly rates for the specific on-peak or off-peak hour of CHILLS usage. The hourly charges
will be calculated using hourly kilowatts as stated in Section 1 of Schedule 15. The total Schedule
11 zonal charge in any month for usage up to the CHILLS Reserved Capacity will not exceed the
Schedule 11 point-to-point zonal monthly rate times the amount in kilowatts of CHILLS Reserved
Capacity in such month. The total Schedule 11 region-wide charge in any month for usage up to the
CHILLS Reserved Capacity will not exceed the Schedule 11 point-to-point region-wide rate times
the amount of kilowatts of CHILLS Reserved Capacity in such month.

       8.      Resales: Resales are not permissible for CHILLS.
